Mon Nov 9courts

Supreme Court lets border wall construction resume in Texas' Big Bend region

The Supreme Court on Monday granted the Trump administration's request to pause a federal judge's injunction that had halted border barrier construction in the Big Bend region of Texas, including Big Bend National Park, with only Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson saying she would have denied the request.

Mon Nov 9courts

Federal judge dismisses Justice Department suit against a Montgomery County, Maryland, gun law

U.S. District Judge Theodore Chuang on Monday dismissed with prejudice a Justice Department lawsuit challenging a Montgomery County, Maryland, law that restricts carrying firearms in places of public assembly and within a 100-yard buffer around them, the Maryland Daily Record and Bethesda Today reported.

Fri Nov 6courts

Judge issues 14-day block on construction of Trump's Washington arch

U.S. District Judge Tanya Chutkan granted a 14-day temporary restraining order on Nov. 5 barring construction, excavation and related work on President Donald Trump's proposed triumphal arch in Washington after the National Capital Planning Commission approved the project, AP, USA Today and The Guardian reported.

Fri Nov 6courts

Seattle judge blocks DOJ from forcing Washington to set aside alleged noncitizen ballots

U.S. District Judge Jamal Whitehead issued a two-week temporary restraining order barring the Justice Department from demanding that Washington election officials set aside ballots of about 405 voters alleged to be noncitizens, or threatening prosecution for counting them under state law, the Washington State Standard, Politico and a court order said.

Thu Nov 5disaster

Record flooding submerges Georgia-Tennessee border towns; Kemp declares emergency in 4 counties

Heavy overnight rain sent the Toccoa River to a record crest near 18 feet on Thursday, flooding McCaysville, Georgia, and Copperhill, Tennessee, prompting dozens of rescues as Gov. Brian Kemp declared a state of emergency in four North Georgia counties, officials and AP said.

Thu Nov 5immigration

Court filings show U.S. held talks with Iran on deporting Iranians during the war

Court documents unsealed Thursday show the Trump administration held talks with Iran about deporting Iranians even while the countries were at war, and a federal judge ordered advance notice before any such removals, AP and ABC News reported.

Thu Nov 5immigration

Justice Department sues Penn State over in-state tuition for undocumented students

The Justice Department on Thursday sued Pennsylvania State University, challenging a policy that grants in-state tuition to undocumented students and seeking to block the practice, the department said.

Wed Nov 4courts

3M agrees to pay up to $7.35 billion to settle PFAS personal injury claims over firefighting foam

3M said it will pay $7.35 billion over nine years, with a present value of $5.8 billion, to resolve personal injury claims over PFAS chemicals in federal litigation centered on firefighting foam, according to the company and AP.

Wed Nov 4immigration

Judge temporarily blocks deportation of detained Afghans to Afghanistan or Pakistan

U.S. District Judge Valerie Caproni on Tuesday temporarily barred the Trump administration from deporting Afghans held in U.S. immigration detention to Afghanistan or Pakistan, in an order that runs through Saturday, AP and ABC News reported.

Wed Nov 4public-safety

Three dead, including the suspect, and two deputies critically wounded in shooting near Spokane

Two Spokane County sheriff's deputies were critically wounded and three people, including the suspected shooter, died after a domestic violence call near Spangle, Washington, on Tuesday, Sheriff John Nowels said, according to The Spokesman-Review and AP.

Mon Nov 2aviation

NTSB says jet that crashed in Florida, killing 9, may have broken up before impact

A Learjet 60 that crashed Sunday in Palm Beach County, Fla., killing all nine people aboard, showed signs of breaking up before impact, National Transportation Safety Board member Tom Chapman said Monday, according to NBC News and AP.

Mon Nov 2courts

Snap settles teen social media addiction case, ending Los Angeles bellwether trial before opening statements

Snap, the parent of Snapchat, reached a confidential settlement Monday with two plaintiffs who say they were harmed by social media use as teenagers, resolving a Los Angeles bellwether case days before trial, CBS News and Courthouse News reported.

Mon Nov 2courts

Judge dismisses Justice Department lawsuit seeking Harvard's race-related admissions data

U.S. District Judge Myong Joun in Boston on Monday dismissed a Justice Department lawsuit that sought to force Harvard University to turn over admissions records for an investigation into whether it still considers race, ruling the government sued too soon, Reuters and Courthouse News reported.

Sat Oct 31courts

Virginia and DC sue to stop Trump's proposed 250-foot memorial arch

Virginia and the District of Columbia filed a federal lawsuit on Saturday seeking to halt construction of President Donald Trump's proposed 250-foot (76-meter) arch, the third legal challenge to the project.

Fri Oct 30courts

Texas grand jury indicts ICE officer accused of striking a man with his vehicle in Houston

A Harris County grand jury on Friday indicted U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer Mario Alberto Morales, 33, on a charge of aggravated assault with a deadly weapon, accusing him of driving into a man during an Oct. 10 encounter in Houston, District Attorney Sean Teare said, according to NBC News and CBS News.

Fri Oct 30aviation

Three killed as two helicopters collide in midair near McMinnville, Oregon

Three people were killed when two helicopters, a Robinson R22 and an Airbus AS350B3, collided in midair Thursday afternoon near McMinnville, Ore., the Yamhill County Sheriff's Office said, according to Oregon Public Broadcasting and the BBC.

Fri Oct 30courts

Kentucky appeals judge denies NCAA bid to block about 30 athletes from playing

Kentucky Court of Appeals Judge Sara Walter Combs on Friday denied the NCAA's request for emergency relief from a temporary injunction, leaving about 30 athletes from the high school class of 2022 eligible to play while the case continues, AP and Kentucky Today reported.

Thu Oct 29courts

Judge bars immigration agents in Southern California from stops based on appearing Latino and working class

U.S. District Judge Maame Ewusi-Mensah Frimpong issued a preliminary injunction requiring immigration agents in the Central District of California to have individualized reasonable suspicion before stopping people, ruling they may not rely solely on someone appearing to be Latino and low-income or working class.

Thu Oct 29courts

Judge blocks Medicaid rule narrowing who counts as 'medically frail' under new work requirements

U.S. District Judge Richard Stearns in Boston ruled Thursday that the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services unlawfully narrowed the "medically frail" exemption from Medicaid's new work requirements, siding in part with 25 states and the District of Columbia.

Thu Oct 29public-health

HHS says it won't act against pharmacies compounding six unapproved peptides, including BPC-157, if they meet set conditions

The Department of Health and Human Services announced a draft enforcement-discretion policy saying it does not intend to take action against licensed pharmacies and physicians that compound six peptides not approved by the FDA, if they meet 10 conditions.

Wed Oct 28us

Dolores Huerta, United Farm Workers co-founder and civil rights leader, dies at 96

Dolores Huerta, the labor organizer who co-founded the United Farm Workers union with Cesar Chavez, died Wednesday at her home in Bakersfield, California, at age 96, her family and the Dolores Huerta Foundation announced.

Wed Oct 28immigration

Legal aid groups sue to stop ICE from hiding locations of detainees with final deportation orders

Four immigrant legal services groups sued the Department of Homeland Security and ICE in federal court in Boston on Wednesday, challenging a September policy that stopped disclosing the locations of detainees who have final orders of removal.

Wed Oct 28courts

Appeals court strikes down West Virginia law shielding judges' and officers' home addresses

The 4th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals ruled Tuesday that West Virginia's version of Daniel's Law, which bars publishing the home addresses and unpublished phone numbers of judges and law enforcement officers, violates the First Amendment.

Wed Oct 28courts

Minnesota man sentenced to 30 years in Feeding Our Future child nutrition fraud

A federal judge in Minneapolis on Wednesday sentenced Salim Said, co-owner of the former Safari Restaurant, to 30 years in prison for his role in the Feeding Our Future scheme to defraud federally funded child nutrition programs, MPR News and AP reported.

Tue Oct 27courts

Supreme Court declines to restore rule letting immigration judges pause some deportation cases

The Supreme Court on Tuesday denied a request from three cities and an immigrant legal services group to revive a 2024 rule that let immigration judges temporarily close some deportation cases, leaving in place a court-approved agreement between Texas and the Justice Department that threw the rule out.

Tue Oct 27immigration

Alex Pretti's parents ask Justice Department to share evidence in his fatal shooting by federal agents

The parents of Alex Pretti, a U.S. citizen and ICU nurse fatally shot by federal immigration officers in Minneapolis in January, said Tuesday that the Justice Department has ignored their requests for information and urged it to share all evidence with Minnesota investigators.

Tue Oct 27public-safety

NTSB calls for safety standards for uncrewed boats after Lake Erie collision

The National Transportation Safety Board issued six recommendations Tuesday to make uncrewed surface vessels easier to detect and more closely monitored, after finding that a NOAA research drone boat that collided with a recreational boat on Lake Erie in 2024 was hard to see and inadequately watched.

Tue Oct 27public-safety

Utah officials link Ted Bundy to 1974 killing of 17-year-old Melissa Ann Smith through DNA

Utah authorities said Tuesday that DNA evidence and other findings show serial killer Ted Bundy was responsible for the 1974 killing of 17-year-old Melissa Ann Smith, and the Summit County Attorney's Office approved closing the cold case.

Mon Oct 26disaster

Four Corners flooding leaves one dead as sewage risks and power outages slow recovery

Parts of the Four Corners region remained under flood warnings Monday as residents began cleaning up after days of heavy rain, and officials reported one flood-related death in Santa Fe, New Mexico.

15-year-old charged in Florida A&M homecoming shooting; prosecutor will seek adult trial

Tallahassee police said Monday that a 15-year-old boy has been charged in Saturday's shooting near Florida A&M University's football stadium that wounded 11 people after the homecoming game.

Friday · Oct 23, 2026 · US Digest · disaster

Four Corners flooding forces rooftop rescues and evacuations in Colorado and New Mexico

Severe flooding along the San Juan and Animas rivers prompted rescues by boat, helicopter and amphibious vehicle in San Juan County, New Mexico, where a county spokesman told the AP that crews were pulling people from roofs and from homes with 3 to 4 feet of water inside. About 600 households in Farmington were told to evacuate, a city spokesperson said, and the county opened a shelter at McGee Park.

In Colorado, Gov. Jared Polis declared a disaster emergency in 11 southwestern counties late Thursday, authorizing the Colorado National Guard to support evacuations and search and rescue, according to the state's emergency management division.
